---
name: analyze-service-boundaries
description: Compare legal, regulatory, funding, planning, watershed, and practical delivery boundaries without collapsing them into one “service area.”
---

# Analyze service boundaries

1. Inventory every use of “service area,” “area of use,” “district,” “sphere,”
   “watershed,” “beneficiary area,” and “delivery area.”
2. Assign each boundary a kind: DDW service description, district jurisdiction,
   LAFCo sphere, County permit eligibility area, grant beneficiary area,
   watershed, parcel set, or practical operating area.
3. Record the creating authority, instrument, date, geometry source, accuracy,
   and intended effect.
4. Acquire GIS data where possible. Georeference image-only exhibits and retain
   the original map.
5. Overlay boundaries, parcels, facilities, wells, hydrants, and delivery
   points in one coordinate system.
6. Flag bisected parcels and boundary conflicts rather than resolving them by
   assumption.
7. Ask whether a boundary requires annexation, sphere amendment, out-of-area
   service approval, permit amendment, or grant approval.

The output must state which boundary answers which question. Never refer to
“the service area” without a qualifier.
